lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: This is the richest man who has ever lived.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In June 2026, he became the first trillionaire in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And eighteen years earlier, he was borrowing money from friends to pay his rent.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Rockets that exploded. A car company bleeding cash. A marriage falling apart.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: This is Elon Musk. And this is how he went all in. Again. And again. And again.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Hi! I'm Dagu. I live inside these videos. [laugh] Don't mind me, I just show up when things get weird. And trust me, they get weird.
lines.text: Hi! I'm Dagu. I live inside these videos. Don't mind me, I just show up when things get weird. And trust me, they get weird.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Pretoria, South Africa. 1971.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon is the kid who reads everything. When he runs out of books, he reads the encyclopedia. For fun.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At school he's small, nerdy, and badly bullied. So he hides in computers.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At twelve, he writes a space shooter game called Blastar, and sells it to a magazine for five hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Twelve years old, already selling space stuff. Some things never change.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At seventeen, he leaves for Canada with almost nothing. Then the US. Physics. Economics.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 1995, he starts a PhD at Stanford. He lasts two days.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two days. Some people take longer to return a pair of shoes.
lines.say: Two days. [chuckle] Some people take longer to return a pair of shoes.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Two days?! [surprised] I've had leftovers in my fridge longer than that.
lines.text: Two days?! I've had leftovers in my fridge longer than that.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Because the internet is exploding, and Elon wants in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: With his brother Kimbal, he starts Zip2. Online city guides for newspapers.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Money is so tight, he sleeps in the office and showers at the YMCA.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then in 1999, Compaq buys Zip2 for 307 million dollars. Elon's cut? 22 million.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So naturally, he buys a million dollar McLaren F1. And later crashes it. No insurance.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: A million dollar car. No insurance. [laugh] Bro.
lines.text: A million dollar car. No insurance. Bro.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Next bet. An online bank called X.com.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It merges with a rival, and becomes a little thing called PayPal.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2000, while he's on a plane, the board fires him as CEO.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Fired from your own company while you're in the air. That's cold.
lines.say: Fired from your own company while you're in the air. [sarcastic] That's cold.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But in 2002, eBay buys PayPal for 1.5 billion dollars. Elon walks away with around 180 million.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Any normal person retires to a beach.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon looks at that money and thinks: rockets.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He wants humans on Mars. So he flies to Russia to buy old missiles.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It goes badly. Turns out, can I get a discount on your missiles, is not a great opening line.
lines.say: It goes badly. [chuckle] Turns out, can I get a discount on your missiles, is not a great opening line.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Imagine asking Russia for a coupon code. [sarcastic] Bold move.
lines.text: Imagine asking Russia for a coupon code. Bold move.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: On the flight home, he decides to build his own. SpaceX. 2002.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then he puts millions into a tiny electric car startup called Tesla.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two of the hardest businesses on Earth. At the same time.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Falcon 1, flight one. 2006. It crashes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Flight two. 2007. It fails.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Flight three. August 2008. It fails again.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Tesla's Roadster costs way more to build than anyone planned. Then the financial crisis hits.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His marriage ends. He's borrowing money from friends to pay rent.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He later called 2008 the worst year of his life.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So he takes almost everything he has left, and splits it between both companies.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Enough for one more launch.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: September 28th, 2008. Falcon 1, flight four.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And holy shit. It reaches orbit.
lines.say: And holy {BEEP}. [surprised] It reaches orbit.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Yep, we beeped that. [chuckle] Keep it clean, kids.
lines.text: Yep, we beeped that. Keep it clean, kids.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Days before Christmas, NASA hands SpaceX a 1.6 billion dollar contract.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And on Christmas Eve, at the last possible moment, Tesla's funding comes through.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two companies, saved in the same week.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then he plays fast.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 2012. Dragon becomes the first commercial spacecraft to visit the space station.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Tesla's Model S shows up, and suddenly electric cars are cool.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 2015. A Falcon 9 booster flies to space, comes back, and lands standing up. A rocket that parks itself.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 2018. Falcon Heavy launches his own cherry red Tesla into space, with a dummy in a spacesuit behind the wheel.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It's still out there, looping around the Sun. The most expensive way ever to avoid traffic.
lines.say: It's still out there, looping around the Sun. [chuckle] The most expensive way ever to avoid traffic.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: That dummy has the best seat in the solar system. No traffic. No speed cameras.
lines.text: That dummy has the best seat in the solar system. No traffic. No speed cameras.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then he starts even more companies.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Neuralink, to wire computers into human brains. The Boring Company, to dig tunnels under traffic.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And Starlink. Thousands of satellites, beaming internet down from space.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But not every bet is a rocket. Some are tweets.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2018, he tweets that he might take Tesla private. Funding secured.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It wasn't. Regulators fined him and Tesla 20 million dollars each.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Twenty million dollars. For one tweet. [sigh] Read your tweets twice, people.
lines.text: Twenty million dollars. For one tweet. Read your tweets twice, people.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Same year, his tunnel company sells twenty thousand flamethrowers. Five hundred dollars each.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then he goes on Joe Rogan's podcast.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So, is selling flamethrowers a good idea?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And is it even a real flamethrower?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then why the weird name?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Same podcast, he takes one puff of a joint. On camera.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The next day, Tesla stock drops. Worth it? Probably not.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Was it worth it? Comment below. I'll wait. [chuckle]
lines.text: Was it worth it? Comment below. I'll wait.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then the Cybertruck reveal. Unbreakable glass. His designer throws a metal ball at it. It breaks. On stage. Twice.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Unbreakable glass, they said. [laugh]
lines.text: Unbreakable glass, they said.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then, the most expensive impulse buy in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2022, he offers 44 billion dollars for Twitter. Tries to back out. Then buys it anyway.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He walks into headquarters carrying a sink. Let that sink in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He fires most of the staff, sells the blue checks, and renames the whole thing X.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Meanwhile in Texas, SpaceX is building the biggest rocket ever made. Starship.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The first one, in 2023, blows up. SpaceX calls it a rapid unscheduled disassembly.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Which is engineer for: it blew the fuck up.
lines.say: Which is engineer for: it blew the {BEEP} up.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Rapid unscheduled disassembly. [chuckle] I'm saying that the next time I break a plate.
lines.text: Rapid unscheduled disassembly. I'm saying that the next time I break a plate.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But in October 2024, the booster flies back to the tower, and the tower catches it. With two giant metal arms.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2025, he goes to Washington to run a cost cutting team called DOGE.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hero to some. Villain to others. A few months later, he's out, and fighting with the President in public.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And then comes 2026. The craziest year yet.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: February. SpaceX swallows his AI company, xAI. The biggest merger ever.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: June. SpaceX goes public, and raises 75 billion dollars. The biggest stock market debut in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: By the end of day one, Forbes puts him at around 1.1 trillion dollars. The first trillionaire. Ever.
lines.say: By the end of day one, Forbes puts him at around 1.1 trillion dollars. [surprised] The first trillionaire. Ever.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: A trillion. With a T. [surprised] I tried counting to a trillion once. I got bored at forty.
lines.text: A trillion. With a T. I tried counting to a trillion once. I got bored at forty.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The guy with three crashed rockets and borrowed rent money.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Tesla starts building the Cybercab. No steering wheel. No pedals.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: September 28th. Exactly eighteen years after Falcon 1 reached orbit, Starship finally does the same.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then October. The new Roadster. Almost ten years late.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Zero to sixty in under a second. And it uses SpaceX thrusters to jump over other cars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Production? 2028. Reserving one costs 250 thousand dollars. Just to reserve it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But not every bet pays off.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In the 2026 midterms, he pours more than 445 million dollars into Republican campaigns. More than any donor in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In Texas, his home base, his candidates lose.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His response? Guess my election interfering space lasers didn't work this time.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: Space lasers. [whispering] I'm not touching that one. Moving on.
lines.text: Space lasers. I'm not touching that one. Moving on.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And his fortune has already slipped back under a trillion. Around 868 billion dollars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Which, let's be honest, is still a lot of rent money.
lines.say: [chuckle] Which, let's be honest, is still a lot of rent money.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And right now, SpaceX is lining up its next stunt. Catching a booster and a ship, on the same flight.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So, genius or lucky?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Most people who go all in, lose everything. And you never hear about them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon went all in again and again. And he's still sitting at the table.

lines.speaker: DAGU
lines.say: So, genius or lucky? Tell me in the comments. And follow, I'll be in the next one too. Bye!
lines.text: So, genius or lucky? Tell me in the comments. And follow, I'll be in the next one too. Bye!
